sentences.text:
Smt Dolly Alias Riya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9
January, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:539
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani
 On The 9 th Of January, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 14174 of 2024
 Smt Dolly Alias Riya
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Rajesh Kumar Sukla - learned counsel for the appl
 Shri Saket Udeniya - learned Public Prosecutor for the
 respondent/State.

Order 
1.

This is the third application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS (439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of bail relating to Crime No.573/2023 registered at Police Station Padav, District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376(2)(n), 376, 363, 366, 370, 323, 506 of I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 3,4,5,7, of Immortal Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956.
The second application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 12.1.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.55598 of 2023.
2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that she forced the prosecutrix to be indulged in prostitution..
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.

As per prosecution story, applicant Dolly @ Riya has taken the prosecutrix to her home where NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:539 2 MCRC-14174-2024 husband of applicant committed rape with prosecutrix and thereafter, applicant and co-accused Raju threatened her.

It is also submitted that other co-accused persons namely Santosh, Chavi, Ashish @
Rajnish, Manisha, Gulnar and Simran have already been granted bail by this Court.
It is also submitted that present applicant is not the wife of co-accused Raju.

Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court to the affidavit of Pushpendra wherein it has been mentioned that Pushpendra is the husband of applicant and in that regard identity card of Election Commission is also filed.

Police itself has depicted that applicant Dolly @ Riya is the wife of late Pushpendra Singh in computer Patrak Proforma No.2; therefore, so far as the prosecution case Smt Dolly Alias Riya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106423754/
1 against applicant - Riya is concerned, no allegation of heinous offence is levelled against her.

sentences.text: Other co-accused persons on similar footing have been granted bail by this Court.
She is in custody since 2.10.2024 and prosecution is failed to examine the prosecutrix before the learned trial Court for a long time.
Today also prosecution has failed to explain that the process issued to the prosecutrix has been served or not.
She cannot be kept in custody for a long time.
She is a lady.
She has no criminal antecedents.
He is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions which may be imposed by the Court.
He is permanent resident of District Morena(M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with prosecution case.
Conclusion of trial will take time.
On these premises, learned counsel prays for bail.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the bail application by submitting that the role of the applicant in the incident is major; therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:539 3 MCRC-14174-2024 it has been prayed to dismiss the bail application.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed, and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-(Rupees One Lac Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
In case, if she is found involved in the offence of same nature, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.
v) The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial;
